source_text: Sed quid faciamus, nisi fraternam infirmitatem feramus et non deficiamus? sudor iste meus credimus quod erit fructuosus. dominus deus noster, qui uoluit ut ueniremus ad uos, qui iussit ut eum quaereremus, qui fecit ut eum interim facie tenus inueniremus, adiutos orationibus uestris faciet nos inuenire cor eius, laetari de concordia eius, gratias agere deo de salute eius, quam non potest habere nisi in ecclesia catholica. extra catholicam ecclesiam totum potest praeter salutem: potest habere honorem, potest habere sacramenta, potest cantare alleluia, potest respondere \'amen\', potest euangelium tenere, potest in nomine patris et filii et spiritus sancti fidem habere et praedicare, sed nusquam nisi in ecclesia catholica salutem poterit inuenire. transeunt enim omnia ista, fratres mei. modo putat quia magnus erit apud suos, si non consenserit et dictus fuerit martyr partis Donati. absit! tollatur in nomine domini de corde eius iste typhus. nouit et ipse, legit et ipse: si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil mihi prodest. ego non dico: si aliquas iniurias quasi iactet se passum esse pro parte Donati aut aliqua damna terrena, nihil ei prodest. ego plus dico: si patiatur foris inimicum Christi, non catholicum fratrem suum quaerentem salutem eius, sed inimicum Christi si foras patiatur et dicat ei foras ab ecclesia Christi inimicus Christi: \'pone thus idolis, adora deos meos\', et non adorans occidatur ab inimico Christi, sanguinem fundere potest, coronam accipere non potest.
thought_title: Outside the Catholic Church everything except salvation
orientation: Augustine is addressing the congregation about Emeritus, the Donatist bishop present among them, and now turns to the limits of what the Donatist party can possess.
pass_a_gloss: But what should we do, except bear brotherly weakness and not give up? This sweat of mine, we believe, will be fruitful. The Lord our God, who willed that we come to you, who commanded that we seek him, who made it so that we find him for now face to face, helped by your prayers will make us find his heart, rejoice over his concord, give thanks to God for his salvation, which he cannot have except in the Catholic Church. Outside the Catholic Church he can do everything except salvation: he can have honor, he can have sacraments, he can sing alleluia, he can answer 'amen', he can hold the gospel, he can have and preach faith in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, but nowhere except in the Catholic Church will he be able to find salvation. For all these things pass away, my brothers. Now he thinks that he will be great among his own, if he does not agree and is called a martyr of the Donatist party. Far be it! Let this pride be taken away from his heart in the name of the Lord. He himself knows, he himself has read: if I hand over my body so that I burn, but do not have love, it profits me nothing. I do not say: if he boasts that he has suffered some injuries or some earthly losses for the Donatist party, it profits him nothing. I say more: if he suffers outside at the hands of an enemy of Christ, not a Catholic brother seeking his salvation, but if an enemy of Christ outside the church of Christ says to him outside: 'put incense to idols, worship my gods', and he is killed by the enemy of Christ for not worshipping, he can pour out blood, he cannot receive a crown.

choices.why: The phrase means 'as far as the face', i.e. in person, and 'face to face' is the natural English idiom.
Typhus here is metaphorical for swelling arrogance, and 'pride' is the plain English sense.
The crown is the martyr's reward, and 'crown' keeps the concrete image.
The glossary requires 'Donatist party' for pars Donati.

bible_refs.note: si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, caritatem autem non habeam, nihil mihi prodest

pass_b_english: But what can we do except bear our brother's weakness and not give up? I believe this sweat of mine will bear fruit. The Lord our God, who willed that we come to you, who commanded us to seek him, who brought it about that we have found him face to face for now, will help us through your prayers to find his heart, to rejoice in his concord, and to give thanks to God for his salvation—which he cannot have except in the Catholic Church. Outside the Catholic Church he can have everything except salvation. He can have honor, he can have the sacraments, he can sing alleluia, he can answer 'amen,' he can hold the gospel, he can have faith in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit and preach it—but nowhere except in the Catholic Church will he be able to find salvation. All these things pass away, my brothers. Right now he thinks he will be great among his own people if he does not give in and is called a martyr of the Donatist party. God forbid! In the name of the Lord, let that pride be taken from his heart. He knows it himself, he has read it himself: If I hand over my body to be burned, but do not have love, it profits me nothing (1 Corinthians 13:3). I am not saying that if he boasts of having suffered some injuries or some earthly losses for the Donatist party, it profits him nothing. I say more: if he suffers outside at the hands of an enemy of Christ—not a Catholic brother seeking his salvation, but an enemy of Christ—if he suffers outside the Church of Christ and an enemy of Christ says to him, 'Put incense to the idols, worship my gods,' and he refuses to worship and is killed by the enemy of Christ, he can shed blood, but he cannot receive the crown.

problems.why: "sudor" means sweat/toil, but "iste" is demonstrative "this" referring to present situation, not "mine" possessive.
problems.fix: this sweat of mine / this toil of ours

edits.old: I believe this labor of mine will bear fruit.
edits.new: I believe this sweat of mine will bear fruit.

fixed: Changed 'this labor of mine' to 'this sweat of mine' to match 'sudor iste meus' (this sweat of mine).

last_rejected.quote: if he suffers outside at the hands of an enemy of Christ—not a Catholic brother seeking his salvation, but an enemy of Christ—if he suffers outside the Church of Christ
last_rejected.source_quote: si patiatur foris inimicum Christi, non catholicum fratrem suum quaerentem salutem eius, sed inimicum Christi si foras patiatur et dicat ei foras ab ecclesia Christi inimicus Christi
last_rejected.why: The English inserts 'the Church of Christ' where the source has only 'foras' (outside/outside the church). The Latin says 'an enemy of Christ says to him outside, away from [the church],' not 'outside the Church of Christ.'
last_rejected.fix: if outside he suffers at the hands of an enemy of Christ—not a Catholic brother seeking his salvation, but an enemy of Christ—if he suffers outside and an enemy of Christ says to him
last_rejected.ruling: Augustine's 'foras ab ecclesia Christi' means 'outside the Church of Christ'; English correctly renders the phrase, not inserting it.
